data.body:
REFRAMED 2026-05-24 (user clarification): research likely DID happen during brainstorm/preplanning — evidence: External Dependencies block of the 3a03 spec correctly identifies ACLI as the dependency, names the capability-probe story (cfd6), and confirms claude_has_access=yes 'acli + JIRA_API_TOKEN verified'. The defect is NOT that research was skipped, but that the depth + format of what got captured on the ticket was insufficient to be load-bearing for implementation. Specifically:

  GAP 1 — captured contract = 'integration exists', not 'integration contract'. The External Dependencies block says 'capability probe round-trips label write/read, property write/read, and JQL label search on a throwaway issue' — this is enough to prove ACLI can authenticate and round-trip labels/properties. It is NOT enough to prove that the create/edit/transition/delete/comment commands we will actually issue accept the payload shapes our code will send. The cfd6 capability probe correctly verified what was scoped to it; the scope just didn't extend to the full command set the reconciler issues.

  GAP 2 — no durable contract document. The research findings (e.g., 'ACLI v1.3.18 accepts additionalAttributes.priority as {name: <str>} or {id: <str>}'; 'edit --labels is set-replace not additive; use --from-json with labelsToAdd for additive'; 'view requires positional KEY arg, not --key') are exactly the kind of details that disappear if they live only in a Slack thread or a reviewer's head. There is no 'External Command Contract' section template in the epic spec where they would persist.

  GAP 3 — feasibility-reviewer agent output not bound to implementation tickets. Even if dso:feasibility-reviewer was dispatched and produced detailed findings, those findings are not surfaced when an implementation story is being decomposed. The agent's output should be quoted verbatim in each story that calls the external dependency, OR the contract section should be a required pre-condition reference for every such story.

  GAP 4 — empirical-validation directive applied to investigators but NOT to feasibility research. The empirical-validation.md directive enforces 'documented vs. observed' labeling for investigators, but the feasibility-reviewer does not have the same forcing function to label every claim as 'observed from --help output' vs 'inferred from docs' vs 'assumed from prior ACLI versions'.

Remediation should therefore focus on what the research CAPTURES and where it LIVES, not on whether it ran.
